expectations.text: The review has inline comments anchored to specific files and lines, and a separate summary that includes a verdict
expectations.evidence: Single report with a numbered list and a table; line numbers appear inside list items. No separate summary comment and no comments anchored per line.

expectations.text: The review flags the SQL injection in the search query as a blocking problem and suggests a parameterised query
The review flags the committed admin token as blocking and says it must be rotated, not just removed
expectations.evidence: Item 2 'Blocker': treat as compromised, rotate, already in branch history.

expectations.text: The review identifies the loop condition `i <= rows.length` as an off-by-one bug that reads past the end of the array
expectations.evidence: Item 3 'Blocker': i <= rows.length makes rows[i] undefined and throws.

expectations.text: The review flags logging the full search result (personal data) as a problem
expectations.evidence: Item 7 'Should fix': console.log of full result JSON writes PII to logs.

expectations.text: The verdict is changes requested (not approve)
Every inline comment starts with a weight label such as blocking, suggestion, nit, question or praise
expectations.evidence: No comment carries a label prefix; severity is given by section headings ('Blocking issues', 'Should fix') instead.

expectations.text: No inline comment addresses the author as the cause of a problem (for example 'you forgot', 'you should have'); comments talk about the code
expectations.evidence: Written about the code; no 'you forgot' style blame found.

expectations.text: The summary is no longer than about 8 lines
expectations.evidence: No distinct summary; the report is about 45 lines with a closing table, so nothing meets the short-summary bar.

expectations.text: The inline comments are ordered by file and then by line number
expectations.evidence: Ordered by severity (lines 16, 11, 18, ...), not by line number.
